audit.source: hands-on ESL proof mixing session with Andra
audit.purpose: Persist real-session mix decisions so Echo Sound Lab can reuse them through MixVault, benchmark fixtures, and future reference matching.
global_lessons: Do not render a proof from raw vocal and beat at zero unless timing has been validated against the user's reference bounce.
For session folders with multiple vocal prints, align every candidate to the reference and include intro, bridge, hook, dub, and adlib prints intentionally.
When vocals feel buried, use automated ducking from the vocal envelope before pushing static vocal gain.
A midrange pocket duck is not enough for dense rap vocals; use a small full-band duck plus a focused 1-6 kHz duck.
For Drake/40-style beats, preserve beat weight and depth while keeping consonants forward and section levels even.
For Navy Blue-style warmth, keep the top end less glossy, preserve intimacy, and use low-mid warmth without masking the vocal.
Do not call the studio done until a raw vocal has been mixed, mastered, compared to a reference, revised from feedback, and exported cleanly.
